While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable. Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest. We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an explicit family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of sub-exponential size. This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.

items.title: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
items.summary: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $ε$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

items.title: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
items.summary: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.

items.title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
items.summary: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imathπ/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quantum Riemannian geometry, we construct a natural Einstein--Hilbert action and hence new quantum gravity models on $A_3,D_4,\widetilde D_4,\widetilde D_5,\widetilde D_6,\widetilde E_6$ in a functional integral approach, other than the 4-star $\widetilde D_4$ which we revisit.

items.title: An algorithm for solving structured problems involving $L$-infimal convolutions
items.summary: We develop an operator-splitting framework for solving structured minimization problems involving linear compositions of $L$-infimal convolutions. We introduce a primal-dual shadow Douglas-Rachford splitting method and establish its convergence. As a result, we derive a fully primal-dual splitting algorithm for the class of the aforementioned minimization problems.

items.title: A General Inequality for Walks in Graphs
items.summary: Let $G$ be a graph and $w_k(G)$ denote the number of walks in $G$ of length $k$. For sequences $a_1, \cdots, a_n$ and $b_1, \cdots, b_n$ of non-negative integers such that $a_1 + \cdots + a_n = b_1 + \cdots + b_n$, we determine a simple necessary and sufficient condition on $a_1, \cdots, a_n, b_1, \cdots, b_n$ for the inequality \[ w_{a_1}(G) \cdots w_{a_n}(G) \geq w_{b_1}(G) \cdots w_{b_n}(G) \] to hold for any graph $G$.

items.title: Sparse optimal control for a class of infinite-dimensional bilinear systems: optimality conditions and uniqueness
items.summary: We study optimal control of an evolution equation in which a scalar control multiplies a bounded operator acting on the state, with free dynamics given by a $C_0$-semigroup. The cost combines tracking terms, a quadratic control cost and an $L^1$ term promoting sparsity in time. We prove existence, derive optimality conditions, and show that optimal controls are thresholded functions of a switching function whose derivative is governed by the commutator of the drift and control operators. Consequently, commuting problems with a terminal cost admit no temporally sparse controls. The $L^1$ term also matters for uniqueness: two distinct controls satisfying the optimality conditions differ on a set of measure bounded from below, contained in the union of their supports, which yields, for the first time, uniqueness for every horizon in stable problems steered to zero. Second-order sufficient conditions and experiments on a bilinear heat equation complete the study.

items.title: Time-Delayed Transformers for Data-Driven Modeling of Low-Dimensional Dynamics
items.summary: We propose the time-delayed transformer (TD-TF), a simplified transformer architecture for data-driven modeling of unsteady spatio-temporal dynamics. TD-TF bridges linear operator-based methods and deep sequence models by showing that a single-layer, single-head transformer can be interpreted as a nonlinear generalization of time-delayed dynamic mode decomposition (TD-DMD). The architecture is deliberately minimal, consisting of one self-attention layer with a single query per prediction and one feedforward layer, resulting in linear computational complexity in sequence length and a small parameter count. Numerical experiments demonstrate that TD-TF matches the performance of strong linear baselines on near-linear systems, while significantly outperforming them in nonlinear and chaotic regimes, where it accurately captures long-term dynamics. Validation studies on synthetic signals, unsteady aerodynamics, the Lorenz '63 system, and a reaction-diffusion model show that TD-TF preserves the interpretability and efficiency of linear models while providing substantially enhanced expressive power for complex dynamics.

items.title: New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
items.summary: We study extremal densities of measurable subsets of metric spaces avoiding prescribed finite geometric configurations. We prove two new upper bounds for three-point avoidance problems: a measurable subset of $S^2$ containing no orthonormal basis has normalized spherical measure at most $7/11$, and a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing no unit equilateral triangle has upper Banach density at most $9/16$. The first bound appears to be the first improvement over the trivial averaging bound for this problem, while the second improves the previously best known upper bound. The proofs are applications of the geometric fractional chromatic number method introduced by Ambrus et al. For this purpose, we formulate the method in a framework that applies both to compact homogeneous spaces and to Euclidean spaces with upper Banach density.

items.title: Spectral Classification of Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
items.summary: We study the unscaled empirical singular spectra of deterministic skew Hilbert--Schmidt kernels evaluated on independent isotropic rows satisfying a uniform quadratic-form variance bound. For arbitrary varying kernels at spatial dimension $d$, tightness and collapse to zero are characterized by boundedness and vanishing, respectively, of the rescaled quadratic energy remaining after deletion of $\lfloor\varepsilon d\rfloor$ leading skew pairs, for every $\varepsilon>0$. A regularized positive-covariance detector proves the necessary direction without a spectral envelope and retains diffuse energy across arbitrarily many small modes. On this exact tightness class, a weighted deterministic source characterizes all probability limits of the empirical spectra through the classical canonical parametrization of symmetric freely infinitely divisible laws. For a fixed kernel, convergence of one bounded resolvent response to a positive deterministic limit, convergence of one normalized logarithmic determinant, and full empirical spectral convergence are each equivalent to a critical Weyl law; the limit is necessarily a possibly degenerate half-Cauchy law. Finally, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for polygonal Brownian Lévy-area spectra to recover the continuous-time bulk under arbitrary deterministic time partitions, even when the normalized mean-square matrix error diverges.

items.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampère equations in big classes
items.summary: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampère equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact Kähler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,α}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.

items.title: The Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem
items.summary: In a previous paper, the authors established the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem, which generalizes the Stone-von Neumann Theorem in quantum mechanics and yields a classification of all unitary Heisenberg representations of an abelian elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system up to unitary equivalence. In this sequel to that paper, we establish an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem in the setting of real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical systems. Firstly, we generalize Stone's Theorem to secure a one-to-one correspondence between the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and the regular self-adjoint densely defined operators on a Hilbert $ C^{\ast} $-module. Secondly, we define the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations and the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system. Thirdly, we construct a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary Heisenberg representation and the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, providing a rigorous two-way passage--which we call ``Heisenberg differentiability-integrability''--between the global unitary formulation of Heisenberg covariance and its infinitesimal formulation in terms of regular self-adjoint densely defined operators. This allows us to prove the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: For a real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation is a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation. Lastly, we obtain explicit descriptions of the position and momentum operators for a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system and construct a natural common invariant core of analytic vectors for them. All requisite technical domain and integrability issues are fully accounted for.

items.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
items.summary: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

items.title: A Taxonomy of Numerical Differentiation Methods
items.summary: Differentiation is a cornerstone of computing and data analysis in every discipline of science and engineering. Indeed, most fundamental physics laws are expressed as relationships between derivatives in space and time. However, derivatives are rarely directly measurable and must instead be computed, often from noisy, potentially corrupt data streams. There is a rich and broad literature of computational differentiation algorithms, but many impose extra constraints to work correctly, e.g. periodic boundary conditions, or are compromised in the presence of noise and corruption. It can therefore be challenging to select the method best-suited to any particular problem. Here we review a broad range of numerical methods for calculating derivatives, present important contextual considerations and choice points, compare relative advantages, and provide basic theory for each algorithm in order to assist users with the mathematical underpinnings. This serves as a practical guide to help scientists and engineers match methods to application domains. We also provide an open-source Python package, PyNumDiff, which contains a broad suite of methods for differentiating noisy data.

items.title: Divisible design graphs from a construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups
items.summary: In this paper, we present a new construction of divisible design graphs with new parameters, obtained by plugging a difference set into a known construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs of diameter 3 that is based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups.

items.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
items.summary: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a new relative BFK type gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles and discuss some extremal properties.

items.title: Discontinuity-Aware Solvers for Vapor-Compression Cycles
items.summary: Physics-based models of vapor-compression cycles are often formulated as large, stiff DAE systems with derivative discontinuities introduced at the points of phase change. We use an implementation of a discontinuity-aware ODE and DAE solver scheme that uses domain-specific, user-declared information to compute appropriate time steps for more efficient integration. This scheme is made open-source within Julia's DifferentialEquations package. We demonstrate how discontinuity information can be specified symbolically in a declarative modeling language such as Dyad and passed to the solver to address the numerical challenges posed. We apply this discontinuity-aware technique to two applications: first, a scalar ODE with two discontinuities, and then a model of a full vapor-compression cycle. The discontinuity-aware solver yields significantly fewer step rejections and improved solver times, particularly with the Rodas5P solver at loose tolerances, as compared to standard error control, suggesting that exposing physical discontinuity information from equation-oriented models to adaptive solvers can improve practical simulation performance without requiring reassembly of the model.

items.title: Well-posedness of compressible $2D$ nonlinear transport equations and quasiconformal maps
items.summary: We prove uniqueness of solutions to a class of nonlinear transport equations in the plane, for which the velocity field is obtained as the convolution of the classical Cauchy kernel with the unknown. Even though the initial datum is bounded and compactly supported, the velocity field may have unbounded divergence. The proof relies on the theory of quasiconformal mappings.

items.title: First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons
items.summary: We develop a first order calculus based on the geometry of realised diameter graphs for perimeter maximisation among convex equilateral small polygons. Polygon side equalities and active diameter constraints define a linearised feasible cone and an associated equality space. We prove that an equilateral small polygon is a strict local maximiser of perimeter modulo Euclidean motions if a multiplier balance holds with strictly positive active diameter multipliers and the active equality space consists only of infinitesimal Euclidean motions. The proof uses a local Euclidean slice and a geometric limiting argument and requires neither independence of the active constraint gradients nor second order information. As an application, we combine our criterion with validated interval arithmetic to establish strict local maximality for Bingane and Audet's polygons $A_{16}$, $A_{32}$, $A_{64}$ and for reconstructions of their polygons $Z_{32}$ and $Z_{64}$. For each $n\in\{32,64\}$, the perimeter of $Z_n$ is strictly larger than that of $A_n$. Thus, strict local maximisers with different perimeters coexist in the space of convex equilateral small polygons with the same number of sides.

items.title: Associative Log Rings and their Bimodules
items.summary: We propose a definition of associative log rings. The role of the commutative monoid is replaced by a variant of a crossed module whose source is a monoid, and we use the resulting group action to control the failure of commutativity. This extends the classical notion of a log ring, even in the commutative case. Natural examples include algebras of logarithmic differential operators. The definition lends itself to a canonical construction of a log enveloping algebra and hence of log bimodules, and we prove that the resulting second log Hochschild cohomology group classifies log square-zero extensions. Along the way, we complete the logarithmic analog of Quillen's classification of abelian group objects in augmented algebras: In exact augmented associative log rings, abelian group objects recover log bimodules. Our constructions enjoy animated analogs, and we develop the basic theory of associative animated log rings \emph{en route} to our classification of exact log square-zero extensions.

items.title: Regularity of velocity averages in kinetic equations with heterogeneity
items.summary: This study investigates the regularity of kinetic equations with spatial heterogeneity. Recent progress has shown that velocity averages of weak solutions $h$ in $L^p$ ($p>1$) are strongly $L^1_{\text{loc}}$ compact under the natural non-degeneracy condition. We establish regularity estimates for equations with an $\boldsymbol{x}$-dependent drift vector $\mathfrak{f} = \mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbolλ)$, which satisfies a quantitative version of the non-degeneracy condition. We prove that $(t,\boldsymbol{x}) \mapsto \int ρ(\boldsymbolλ) h(t,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbolλ)\, d\boldsymbolλ$, for any sufficiently regular $ρ(\cdot)$, belongs to the fractional Sobolev space $W_{\text{loc}}^{β,r}$, for some regularity $β\in (0,1)$ and integrability $r \geq 1$ exponents. While such estimates have long been known for $\boldsymbol{x}$-independent drift vectors $\mathfrak{f}=\mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbolλ)$, this is the first quantitative regularity estimate in a general heterogeneous setting. As an application, we obtain a regularity estimate for entropy solutions to heterogeneous conservation laws with nonlinear flux and $L^\infty$ initial data.

items.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
items.summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

items.title: The profinite shape equivalence
items.summary: We show that, for every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{X}$, the profinite shape induces a canonical equivalence between the $\infty$-category of pro-objects in locally constant constructible sheaves of anima in $\mathcal{X}$ and the slice $\infty$-category of profinite anima over the profinite shape $\widehatΠ_{\infty}(\mathcal{X})$. We deduce this profinite shape equivalence from the monodromy classification theorem by establishing a continuous version of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence for profinite anima. In addition, we explain how the monodromy classification theorem recovers its classical counterparts concerning locally constant sheaves of finite sets and of (abelian) groups.

items.title: Large diameter growth for vortex patches
items.summary: For every $N>0$, the 2D incompressible Euler equation admits a smooth, simply connected vortex patch initially contained in the unit disk whose diameter exceeds $N$ at some finite time. We discover a point-vortex mechanism in which a bounded motion of three equal positive vortices drives a passive particle outward through successive transitions. A finite-time point-vortex approximation transfers the resulting separation to a single simply connected patch.

items.title: The internal languages of univalent categories
items.summary: Internal language theorems are fundamental in categorical logic, since they express an equivalence between syntax and semantics. One such theorem was proven by Clairambault and Dybjer, who corrected the result originally by Seely. More specifically, they constructed a biequivalence between the bicategory of locally Cartesian closed categories and the bicategory of democratic categories with families with extensional identity types, $Σ$-types, and $Π$-types. This theorem expresses that the internal language of locally Cartesian closed categories is extensional Martin-Löf type theory with dependent sums and products. In this paper, we study the theorem by Clairambault and Dybjer for univalent categories, and we extend it to various classes of toposes, among which are $Π$-pretoposes, elementary toposes, and elementary toposes with a universe. The results in this paper have been formalized using the proof assistant Rocq and the UniMath library.

items.title: Identifiability of latent variable models with flexible latent distributions
items.summary: Latent variable models are popularly used to characterize dependence among many observed variables through underlying latent variables. Recent advances in statistics and machine learning methods have encouraged growing interest in studying latent variable models with flexible latent distributions that capture complex latent structures. This flexibility, however, raises a fundamental question of whether model parameters can be identified when the latent distribution is unknown and must itself be learned. In this paper, we show that exact identifiability fails almost everywhere, in the sense that distinct but arbitrarily close pairs of model parameters and latent distributions can yield exactly the same distribution for the observed variables. Nonetheless, the resulting identification ambiguity is small. In particular, we prove that the identification ambiguity, measured by the diameter of the set of parameters inducing the same marginal distribution, vanishes at a superpolynomial rate of $\exp\{-c(\log p)^2\}$ as the number of observed variables $p$ grows. Building on this result, we show that the failure of exact identifiability need not preclude consistent estimation or valid inference of the model parameters and latent distribution. These results suggest that, when many variables are observed, the identifiability issue is far less of an obstacle to estimation and inference in latent variable models than is commonly expected.

items.title: Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development
items.summary: Neurons receive information through their dendrites. During development, when synaptic connections are forming, dendrites grow, retract, and branch. The resulting dendritic tree shapes the structure of the broader neural network. Crucially, retraction and branching make it necessary to track whole dendritic paths rather than only their endpoints. While this is handled implicitly in some existing simulations, here we construct an explicitly path-valued stochastic process for dendrite growth. Combining this with a branching process, using ideas from measure-valued branching particle systems, we show that the model produces the typical tree structures of real dendrites. To complement this analytical work, we also outline several methods for numerical simulation, including time discretisations at different temporal scales and an approximation using a dynamic graph. This provides both a more rigorous mathematical framework and more structured simulation methods for modelling dendrite development.

items.title: Seaweed algebras with restricted part sizes
items.summary: Seaweed algebras are a class of Lie algebras that are naturally characterized by a pair of compositions, which in turn are represented visually as planar graphs called meanders. These meanders provide a straightforward method for computing the index of the associated algebra. The goal of this paper is to enumerate those seaweed algebras with a fixed index and whose associated compositions have restricted part sizes. In particular, we enumerate those with composition part sizes from so-called acyclic sets. We also establish a bijection between sets of indecomposable seaweed algebras with meanders with certain restricted part sizes and sets of permutations with restricted displacements. In certain cases, the index of the algebra can be determined by a simple statistic on the permutation.

items.title: Compensation Formulas for Branching Lévy Processes
items.summary: This paper aims to establish two compensation formulas for branching Lévy processes. The first expresses expected sums over spatial jumps as integrals against the Lévy measure, with the future family of the jumping particle started from its position immediately after the jump. The second expresses expected sums over reproduction events as time integrals weighted by the branching rate and the offspring distribution, with each event marked by the ordered tuple of branching processes initiated by its offspring. Combined with the fixed-time many-to-one formula, it recovers the whole-tree many-to-one identity for functionals of ancestral spatial paths.

items.title: Higher-Derivative Conjectures of Sendov
items.summary: We prove Conjectures~3 and~8 of Sendov's 2002 survey and deduce Conjecture~9. More precisely, let $p$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. For every integer $s$ with $1\le s<n$, we prove that each zero of $p$ lies within distance $2s/(s+1)$ of a zero of $p^{(s)}$. For quartics, we obtain the sharp bound $2/\sqrt3$ for the second derivative and determine all polynomials attaining it.

items.title: Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
items.summary: Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. We propose an implicit-explicit (IMEX) finite element scheme with inf-sup stable elements, prove its unconditional long-time stability, and show for the spatially semi-discrete scheme that the error reaches a prescribed tolerance in finite time. Our analysis also suggests that the non- linear nudging term requires the mesh resolution to be fine enough (${χ= O(H^{-1})}$, where $χ$ is the nonlinear nudging intensity and ${H}$ is the observation mesh size). Further, our error estimates suggest that a larger nonlinear exponent $γ$ requires finer observational resolution, which is confirmed by numerical tests. Numerical experiments, including two-dimensional forced viscous flow in a periodic box, flow past a cylinder, and flow over a flat plate, show that nonlinear nudging synchronizes with the true solution considerably faster than linear nudging. We also show that observations in a subregion suffice to synchronize the whole flow

items.title: The orbital architecture of 14 Herculis system as a KAM-stable three-body configuration
items.summary: The 14 Herculis system hosts two massive giant planets on eccentric and mutually inclined orbits, making it a compelling test case for long-term stability in the spatial planetary three-body problem. We develop an analytical description of its dynamics using averaging, symplectic reduction of symmetries and KAM theory. For parameters compatible with the observed architecture, the secular quadrupole Hamiltonian possesses two elliptic relative equilibria that organise the nearby dynamics. The octupole contribution introduces a second slow angle and yields a properly-degenerate multiscale Hamiltonian. Under the corresponding smallness, non-resonance, and non-degeneracy conditions, families of quasi-periodic orbits coming from the relative equilibria of the quadrupolar approximation fill invariant 2-tori. Restoring the two fast mean anomalies and the cyclic angle conjugate to the angular-momentum, and considering the full system, produce two Cantor families of five-dimensional quasi-periodic tori in the reconstructed planetary problem. These invariant structures provide a Hamiltonian mechanism for the long-term confinement of eccentric and mutually inclined configurations compatible with 14 Her.

items.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
items.summary: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

items.title: On the $φ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
items.summary: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $φ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

items.title: Invariant flags and integral matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomial
items.summary: We give an asymptotic formula for integral matrices with a prescribed characteristic polynomial in an expanding entry box over a number field. For cyclic matrices, normalized logarithmic covolumes of a primary invariant flag become uniform on a permutohedral chamber. Their joint distribution with the rescaled matrix factors for tests invariant under reflections at the real places. Separating irreducible factors of multiplicities \(e_i\) into distinct translates multiplies the leading coefficient by \(\prod_i e_i!\). We also bound every noncyclic rational type.

items.title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
items.summary: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions associated with polynomial sequences satisfying a first-order differential recurrence. As applications, we prove weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials, several families of Eulerian polynomials, the Bell polynomials, and the reflected generalized Laguerre polynomials. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai concerning the Bell and Laguerre polynomials.

items.title: An application of "Selmer group Chabauty" to arithmetic dynamics
items.summary: We describe how one can use the "Selmer group Chabauty" method developed by the author to show that certain hyperelliptic curves of the form $$ C \colon y^2 = x^{2g+1} + h(x)^2 \,, $$ with $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $\operatorname{deg} h \le g$ and $h(0)$ is odd, have only the "obvious" rational points $\infty$ (the unique point at infinity on the smooth projective model of the curve) and $(0, \pm h(0))$. Let $c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and write $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$. We denote the iterates of $f_c$ by $f_c^{\circ n}$; i.e., we set $f_c^{\circ 0}(x) = x$ and $f_c^{\circ(n+1)}(x) = f_c(f_c^{\circ n}(x))$. As an application of the method, we prove that if $f_c^{\circ 2}$ is irreducible, then $f_c^{\circ 6}$ is also irreducible. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), it also follows that $f_c^{\circ 10}$ is irreducible.

items.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
items.summary: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link which is not Lorenz, thereby disproving the Birman--Kofman conjecture that every horseshoe link is a Lorenz link. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.

items.title: A singularity detecting uniformly convergent quantum wavelet framework for weakly singular nonlocal Emden--Fowler systems with quantum Mittag--Leffler sources
items.summary: We develop a quantum wavelet-based computational framework for coupled systems of Caputo-type quantum ($q$-) fractional Emden--Fowler problems with $q$-Mittag--Leffler source terms, where the solutions exhibit singular behavior in time. Here $q\in(0,1)$ denotes the parameter of $q$-calculus. The highest-order Caputo $q$-fractional derivatives are expanded through the Haar wavelet basis, and the lower-order fractional derivatives are approximated through Jackson $q$-fractional integrals of Haar wavelets. The continuous problem reduces to a nonlinear algebraic system on the midpoint collocation points. Under suitable structural assumptions, the Banach fixed-point theorem yields the existence and uniqueness of the continuous solutions and wellposedness of the discrete solutions on collocation points. The nonlinearity of the given problem is dealt with by the damped Newton's iteration. In addition, We prove stability of the scheme and derive rigorous convergence estimates in a weighted norm that remains uniformly controlled despite the appearance of singular weight at $t=0$ in the continuous model. When the highest-order fractional derivatives are Hölder continuous with exponent $σ$, the mathematical error of weakly singular solution and its lower-order fractional derivatives become $\mathcal{O}(τ_L^σ)$, where $τ_L=2^{-(L+1)}$ denotes the width of the finest subintervals for maximum level of resolution $L$. First-order convergence is guaranteed under stronger regularity with $σ=1$. Several test cases are considered to confirm the accuracy and robustness of the present approach, which strongly agrees with the theoretical estimates. In particular, first-order convergence is observed even where the stronger regularity assumption is not satisfied.

items.title: An infinite family of bipartite hypotraceable graphs
items.summary: A graph is hypotraceable if it has no Hamiltonian path but every vertex-deleted subgraph does. In 1978, Grötschel asked whether a bipartite hypotraceable graph exists. We resolve this long-standing question in a strong sense by proving that such graphs exist for every sufficiently large even order. Moreover, we show that bipartite hypotraceable graphs can have $\left(1/4+o(1)\right)n^2$ edges, asymptotically attaining the maximum possible number of edges of a bipartite graph, and that there are at least $2^{(1/4+o(1))n^2}$ nonisomorphic examples of order $n$, as $n$ tends to infinity through even integers. Finally, we prove that every bipartite graph occurs as an induced subgraph of a bipartite hypotraceable graph.

items.title: On the recursive feasibility and stability of MPC without terminal constraints
items.summary: In this paper, we analyze stability and recursive feasibility of a model predictive control (MPC) scheme that does not rely on terminal ingredients -- such as terminal constraints or a terminal cost based on a terminal controller. In the proposed formulation, we augment the cost function by a weighted finite tail which is optimized online, and we show it plays the role of a stabilizing terminal cost. Under a relaxed, local dynamic programming condition on the tail, we certify a family of regions -- parameterized by the tail's weight coefficient -- on which the problem is recursively feasible and the origin is asymptotically stable. These regions are larger as the weight increases: in particular, we show that any state that can be steered within the control horizon to a predefined neighborhood of the origin is contained in a certified region for a sufficiently large weight. Finally, we characterize the closed-loop performance over the certified region, bounding the suboptimality of the closed loop with respect to the infinite-horizon optimal cost. We conclude the discussion by illustrating these results on a simple numerical example.

items.title: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
items.summary: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.

items.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
items.summary: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.

items.title: Algorithms for experimenting with Zariski dense matrix groups over number fields
items.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be an algebraic number field. We provide a computational analog of the strong approximation theorem for finitely generated Zariski dense groups $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{P})$, $n$ prime. That is, we present algorithms to find the set of congruence quotients of $H$ modulo all maximal ideals of a finitely generated subring $R$ of $\mathbb{P}$ such that $H\leq \mathrm{SL}(n,R)$. The algorithms have been implemented in GAP. Potential applications are illustrated by a range of experiments in degree $2$, with a special focus on Bianchi groups.

items.title: Generalized and Convex Poincaré Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
items.summary: We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $χ^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincaré inequality and quadratic transport-$χ^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $χ_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities by identifying sharp conditions on the behavior of the density both at infinity and near isolated zeros. We show that when $q'>p'$, the concentration behavior becomes polynomial rather than exponential at infinity. Finally, we interpret these inequalities through the lens of optimization in Wasserstein space. In particular, the equivalence between transport-divergence and Poincaré inequalities appears as an analogue of the equivalence between quadratic growth and Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequalities in finite-dimensional optimization.

items.title: On Green's Conjecture for Curves on Anticanonical Surfaces
items.summary: We prove Green's conjecture for smooth curves $C$ on rational surfaces $X$ such that $-K_X|_C$ is effective on $C$. In addition, on birationally ruled surfaces $X$ of irregularity $q \geq 1$ carrying an effective anticanonical divisor, we show that Green's conjecture holds for all smooth curves $C$ on $X$ covering the base curve with degree at least $2$, provided the latter has only finitely many gonal pencils or the gonality of $C$ is special with respect to the ruling.

items.title: Complete characterization of graphs with common maximal abelian cover
items.summary: The maximal abelian cover of a connected graph is the quotient of its universal cover by the commutator subgroup of its fundamental group. We provide a complete classification of finite connected graphs with isomorphic maximal abelian covers. For trees or for connected graphs with at least two cycles, the cover determines the base up to isomorphism; in cycle rank one, it determines the primitive cyclic pattern of rooted trees attached to the unique cycle. We also characterize when every automorphism descends to the base and give an orbit-size criterion for splitting the canonical lift extension, answering two questions raised by Baez in 2026.

items.title: Maximality of the Došen-Petrić Boolean Category
items.summary: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Every congruence preserved by the operations on morphisms and by uniform formula substitution either is equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. We give two proofs that use Boolean Coherence and uniform formula substitution to derive equality of the product projections from an identification of distinct parallel morphisms. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

items.title: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
items.summary: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A.Hanlon, J.Hicks, and O.Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

items.title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
items.summary: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

items.title: Long-Term Quantile Treatment Effects with Combined Experimental and Observational Data
items.summary: This paper studies the identification, estimation, and inference of long-term quantile treatment effects (LTQTEs) when short-term experimental data are supplemented with long-term observational data. Under a latent unconfoundedness framework, we establish identification of the LTQTE curve and derive the corresponding efficient influence functions. Building on these influence functions, we propose a semiparametrically efficient estimation procedure and develop a multiplier bootstrap method for uniform inference on the LTQTE curve, yielding valid simultaneous confidence bands over a continuum of quantile indices.

items.title: Characterization of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule and lattice points in flagged hive polytopes
items.summary: We have previously, for a given positive integer $n$, explicitly characterized by certain linear inequalities the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux of shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ produced by $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson (LR) rule. We now extend that characterization for lower shape lengths. Then using the composition of promotion operators defining the Naito-Suzuki-Watanabe bijection between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux, we also explicitly characterize by certain linear inequalities the corresponding $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux when the shape length is $2n$ or $2n-1$. In addition, when the given $n$ is $3$ or $ 4$ the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and the $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux are characterized by linear inequalities for lower shape lengths. Since recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule are in natural bijection with Littlewood-Richardson-Sundaram (LRS) tableaux, we relate our results on the inverse quantum LR rule with other two bijections for the Naito-Sagaki conjecture and establish bijections between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux, $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux and the lattice points in a (disjoint) union of flagged hive polytopes.

items.title: Residual-Driven Basis and Data Selection for Polynomial Approximation of High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
items.summary: We develop greedy strategies for selecting global polynomial basis functions and training data in the sparse approximation of high-dimensional partial differential equations, with emphasis on Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations arising in nonlinear optimal control. Inspired by the goal-oriented dual-weighted residual framework, we derive a closed-form, mesh-free indicator that predicts, to first order, the reduction of the PDE residual obtained by adding a single candidate basis function, without solving an adjoint problem. In the data-driven regime, we jointly select basis functions and gradient-augmented training samples by maximizing the predicted decrease of a supervised loss. Numerical experiments on benchmark PDEs and nonlinear optimal control problems in up to 35 dimensions show accuracy comparable to non-adaptive approaches with substantially fewer basis functions and training samples.

items.title: Banchoff Curvature and Realisation Moduli of Piecewise-Affine Arrangement Immersions
items.summary: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-Müller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.

items.title: Control and Identification in Least-Squares Self-Tuning Regulation with Unknown Input Gain
items.summary: We study stability, minimum variance tracking and parameter identification for the Åstr{ö}m--Wittenmark self-tuning regulator with unknown input gain. Ordinary least squares (LS) estimates are used directly in certainty-equivalent control. Under the stated plant and martingale noise assumptions, we establish almost sure stability and optimal tracking for every bounded reference, provided that the gain estimates remain nonzero. When at least two parameters are estimated, all coefficient estimates are strongly consistent. The proof obtains a logarithmic information lower bound from an LS energy identity and uses it to establish gain consistency without assuming closed-loop stability. For at least two estimated parameters and every bounded reference, the squared error is almost surely $O(\log\log n/n)$ for the estimated ratios of the plant coefficients to the input gain and $O(\log\log\log n/\log n)$ for the full parameter estimate. A law of the iterated logarithm shows that the latter rate is sharp under zero reference. The bound for the full parameter estimate improves with reference energy, which also appears explicitly in the logarithm law for cumulative squared tracking residuals. These results show that optimal tracking can coexist with substantially slower estimation of the full parameter vector than of the coefficient ratios used in feedback. For at least two estimated parameters, a chi-square limit yields asymptotically exact confidence ellipsoids for every bounded reference.

items.title: Hypersurfaces that are far from ruled
items.summary: We show that a very general complex hypersurface of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^{n+1}$ is not ruled whenever $n\geq3$ and $d\geq2\lceil(n+2)/3\rceil$. This improves Kollár's original degree bound to the bound subsequently obtained by Totaro for stable irrationality and, in particular, includes very general quartic fourfolds. More precisely, we find new bounds for the minimal degree of a dominant rational map from a very general hypersurface to a ruled variety or a conic bundle, improving on previous bounds of Chen--Stapleton. The proofs combine Kollár's reduction to positive characteristic with the Jacobson correspondence for inseparable extensions.

items.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
items.summary: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(β+1)}/β}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $β^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logβ$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $β$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.

items.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
items.summary: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

items.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras
items.summary: In 1990, Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e., bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In the case $n>1$, the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any of the well-known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). We describe the algebra of all derivations of $W(2)$ and the subalgebras of $W(2)$ of codimension one. We also study similar problems for the algebra $W_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $S_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace-zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.

items.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, IV
items.summary: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.

items.title: Smoothing Bias and Direction Recovery at Boundary Minima of the Nuclear Norm along Matrix Lines
items.summary: We study optimal matrix directions associated with minimizing $\|G+λΘ\|_*$, the nuclear norm along a fixed affine line of real matrices with scalar multiplier $λ$. At a rank-deficient minimum, the compact polar factor can violate the tangency constraint even at the minimizing multiplier. Spectral smoothing gives a continuous scalar equation for tangency. We quantify its bias at a unique boundary minimum, where exactly one one-sided derivative vanishes. An orthogonal block decomposition shows that pseudo-Huber smoothing with scale $δ$ shifts the multiplier by exact order $δ^{2/3}$ as $δ\to0$. The Frobenius error relative to the minimum-Frobenius-norm optimal direction has exact order $δ^{1/3}$ when some singular values vanish at exactly second order in the multiplier displacement, and $δ^{2/3}$ otherwise. A sharp rank bound rules out the slower rate when $Θ$ has rank at most two. Huber smoothing gives an error of exact order $δ$ for the same limiting direction. Convergent expansions in powers of $δ^{1/3}$ also yield a three-scale extrapolation with $O(δ)$ error after restoring feasibility.

items.title: Conservative algebras of $2$-dimensional algebras, V
items.summary: The notion of conservative algebras appeared in a paper by Kantor in 1972. Later, he defined the conservative algebra $W(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. If $n>1$, then the algebra $W(n)$ does not belong to any well-known class of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, or Leibniz algebras). It looks like $W(n)$ in the theory of conservative algebras plays a similar role to the role of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the theory of Lie algebras. Namely, an arbitrary conservative algebra can be obtained from a universal algebra $W(n)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ The present paper is a part of a series of papers, which dedicated to the study of the algebra $W(2)$ and its principal subalgebras.

items.title: On Ext-groups between Arthur-type modules of the graded Hecke algebras of type A
items.summary: Let $\mathbb H_n$ be the graded Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. This article establishes a formula for Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and a $W$-type $\mathbb H_n$-module in terms of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain an explicit and efficient method to compute Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and an Arthur-type module of $\mathbb H_n$. In particular, this proves new instances of a conjecture of Chan and Prasad on Ext non-vanishing between Arthur-type representations. We also discuss some other non-Ext vanishing results for calibrated modules.

items.title: Exact factorizations of countable groups into discrete and thin subsets
items.summary: For every countably infinite Hausdorff topological group $G$, we construct an exact factorization $G=AB$, where $A,B\subseteq G$ and every element of $G$ has a unique representation as $ab$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Both factors are infinite, closed, discrete, and thin. A subset $C\subseteq G$ is thin if the intersections $hC\cap C$ and $Ch\cap C$ are finite for every nonidentity element $h\in G$. In any countably infinite group, an exact factorization into two infinite thin subsets can be constructed starting from any partial exact factorization with finite nonempty factors. Given a finite or countably infinite family of infinite subsets of the group, we can choose the extension so that each factor meets every member of the family in infinitely many points. If the topology on the group has a countable base and every nonempty open set is infinite, taking the nonempty members of the base as this family yields dense thin factors.

items.title: Sums and Products in Dynamically Central Syndetic Sets
items.summary: Glasscock and Le introduced the notion \textit{dynamically central syndetic sets} in a minimal topological dynamical system under the minimal action of the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, +).$ In this short note, we introduce these large sets in the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, \cdot)$ and establish that dynamically central syndetic sets contain the Hindman configuration $\{x,y,x+y,xy\}$. Furthermore, we show that there are dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets that do not contain such configurations.

items.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
items.summary: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For a central division $F$-algebras $L$ of a fixed degree $n$ we identify the double quotients of the homogeneous spaces $L_E^\times/L^\times$ with a topological space $Ξ_E$ which does not depend on a choice of $L$ , define a convolution products $\ast _L$ on the space ${\mathcal M} _E$ compactly supported measures on $Ξ_E$ and conjecture that the product $\ast _L$ on $Ξ_E$ does not depend on a choice of $L$.

items.title: Mean Field Games: Large Sparse Network Limits and Laplexion Dynamics
items.summary: Dynamic games are considered with large subpopulations distributed over large sparse graphs, where each agent has mean field coupling with all agents within the same cluster and meanwhile receives impact from neighboring clusters. Tractable limit models are obtained via the network limits of graph Laplacian operators modelling second order interactions. The resulting mean field game (MFG) has what is called Laplexion dynamics. For ring and torus topology cases, solutions for linear quadratic Laplexion MFG systems with infinite populations on infinite node networks are obtained via a second order linear partial differential equation system. This work focusses on the relationship between the finite population model and the sparse network limit model. We prove an $ε$-Nash equilibrium property for the obtained decentralized strategies.

items.title: Binary Affine Optimization with Nearly-Graphic Constraint Matrices
items.summary: We present a polynomial-time algorithm for binary affine optimization with a linear objective when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight at most 2, and prove that the problem is NP-hard when every column of the constraint matrix has Hamming weight exactly 3. We obtain fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms for the unrestricted problem provided that a nearly-graphic certificate is given, where the certificate roughly measures how far the constraint matrix is from having columns of Hamming weight at most 2. We apply our FPT algorithm to Max-Lin$_2$ on graphs and obtain FPT algorithms parameterized by the contraction distance and contraction rank of the graph, utilizing the concept of Eulerian-spanning set. In the case of contraction distance, another FPT algorithm can be used to find the corresponding certificate; that is, we obtain an FPT algorithm that requires no information beyond the problem instance itself.

items.title: Attention's forward pass and Frank-Wolfe
items.summary: We study the hardmax limit of self-attention dynamics for token embeddings obtained in the zero-temperature ($β\to+\infty$) regime, and relate it to the finite-$β$ setting. In this limit, the update rule can be viewed as a Frank-Wolfe step for a quadratic objective over the convex hull of the current token embeddings. When the key-query matrix is negative semidefinite, the method linearly contracts all tokens to a single cluster at the origin. When it is positive semidefinite, extending the hardmax rule to the entire convex hull induces a Voronoi diagram: vertices are stationary, interior points remain in their initial cells, and each token moves along a straight line toward its cell's vertex, yielding (super-)exponential convergence. As a byproduct, we also establish well-posedness of the associated ODE limit in this regime. Returning to the finite-$β$ regime, we model self-attention dynamics as a Markov chain and prove dynamic metastability: with high probability, interior tokens reach near-vertex configurations in a constant number of steps and remain within a small neighborhood for times that grow exponentially in the inverse temperature $β$, before ultimately collapsing to the origin. Thus, the hardmax dynamics accurately approximate the finite-$β$ process over exponentially long time horizons.

items.title: KL-Guided Support Selection and Subspace Cubic Newton Methods for Sparse Optimization
items.summary: We study sparse composite optimization with a smooth loss and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth regularizer. The objective is locally smooth on each fixed support. Our method combines full-space proximal-gradient steps with inexact cubic-regularized Newton steps on a subspace selected by thresholding. If the iterates are bounded and the objective satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property, the entire sequence converges to a first-order stationary point. A threshold based on the KL exponent ensures that the selected coordinate set coincides with the support of the limit after finitely many iterations, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption. We also provide a residual-based threshold when such an exponent exists and its value is unknown. Under an additional continuity assumption on the restricted Hessian, the line search eventually accepts full cubic steps. With bounded cubic regularization parameters and damping parameters chosen to meet the target tolerances, we bound the number of outer iterations needed to reach restricted approximate second-order stationarity after support identification and entry into the full-step regime. We conduct numerical experiments in two settings: when the KL exponent is known and when it is unknown. In the former case, we use a degenerate problem to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. In the latter case, we compare the proposed method and its adaptive variant with existing solvers on sparse recovery and logistic regression problems.

items.title: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem for certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings
items.summary: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem concerns global inversion of continuously differentiable mappings between Banach spaces. Here we consider a weaker notion of smoothness and work with continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings. We prove that a continuously Gateaux differentiable mapping with invertible derivatives such that the inverses are uniformly bounded, possesses a continuous right inverse on every compact set. We also provide sufficient conditions for global invertibility of certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings between Banach spaces.

items.title: Testing the Pareto law through a Stein-Laplace characterization
items.summary: A Stein--Laplace characterization yields two closed-form goodness-of-fit statistics for the Pareto type-I family with unknown shape and known lower endpoint. The signed integral statistic $T_n$ has a standard normal limit after studentization, but explicit non-Pareto alternatives show that it is not omnibus consistent. The integrated squared discrepancy $S_n$ yields a consistent test against every fixed non-Pareto alternative on the specified support with a finite, positive logarithmic moment. We derive the weighted chi-square null limit of $nS_n$ and give conditions for an asymptotically valid parametric-bootstrap and plug-in covariance-operator method. The latter uses Nyström eigenvalue approximation to avoid repeated sample generation and parameter estimation. A large Monte Carlo comparison study shows competitive performance relative to existing procedures in the literature. In the paired study, the two calibrations have similar empirical power, with slightly higher small-sample rejection rates for the bootstrap in some settings. In the timing experiment, covariance-operator calibration is approximately $28$--$37$ times faster at $n=200$. An exploratory threshold-sensitivity analysis of Danish fire-insurance losses illustrates the dependence of Pareto goodness-of-fit conclusions on the specified tail region.

items.title: Pluricanonical locally conformally almost Kähler metrics, circle-invariant $G_2$ structures, and Laplacian flows
items.summary: We study explicit Hodge evolutions of pluricanonical locally conformally almost Kähler metrics and their relation to locally conformal parallel $G_2$ structures. A compact locally conformal parallel $7$-manifold with a parallel non-zero Lee form, carrying a structure-preserving free circle action of constant orbit length orthogonal to the Lee field, has a $6$-dimensional quotient which is pluricanonical with a parallel Lee form and a non-integrable almost complex structure. The fundamental forms upstairs and downstairs are Laplacian eigenforms with an explicit eigenvalue ratio. Conversely, for a fixed normalized $SU(3)$ completion, we characterize the curvature of a circle-invariant locally conformal parallel lift. The lift equations force a pluricanonical base to have parallel Lee form, even locally, and exclude strict integrable pluricanonical bases. Independently, the pluricanonical eigenform identity gives a shrinking solution of He's full Hodge equation and an immortal $d^*d$ solution contracting the Lee plane.

items.title: Global solvability, regularity and exponential convergence in a quasilinear chemotaxis-haptotaxis system with mostly repulsive signal production
items.summary: Motivated by biological and mathematical viewpoints, we systematically investigate the global dynamics of a quasilinear chemotaxis haptotaxis system with mostly repulsive signal production. We show unconditional 2D boundedness, blow up prevention for parabolic-elliptic-ODE case in nD, small data boundedness and exponential convergence under endpoint Lebesgue smallness, and 3D weak-solution eventual regularity. Our findings extend the corresponding repulsive chemotaxis only theory to the chemotaxis haptotaxis setting and demonstrate a positive effect of chemo-repulsion on global dynamics.

items.title: Non-local Transport Geometry for Papangelou Point Processes
items.summary: We develop new analytical tools for the analysis of interacting point processes and their associated dynamics by introducing a non-local Benamou-Brenier-type transport distance tailored to (stationary) Papangelou point processes. Under a suitable Dobrushin-type condition, quantified by a constant $ζ$, we show that the natural spatial birth-and-death dynamics associated with a Papangelou point process is the EVI$(ζ)$-gradient flow of the (specific) relative entropy. Moreover, we establish $ζ$-geodesic convexity of the (specific) relative entropy and derive new functional inequalities, including HWI, Log-Sobolev, and Talagrand inequalities.

items.title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
items.summary: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.

items.title: Round hyperspheres uniquely minimize most tangent-point energies
items.summary: We show that round hyperspheres uniquely minimize a broad class of generalized tangent-point energies among all boundaries of bounded Caccioppoli sets sharing the same perimeter or enclosed volume. This includes closed $C^1$-hypersurfaces. Equivalently, we establish sharp lower bounds for the associated scale-invariant ratios of energy to surface measure and energy to volume, respectively, with equality precisely for round spheres.

items.title: $H^2$-based equilibrated residual error estimates
items.summary: We develop a framework for equilibrated residual a posteriori error analysis of finite element methods, based on decomposing vector- and tensor-valued Sobolev spaces into $H^2$ and $H^1$ spaces. To estimate the residual functional acting on $H^2$ component, the method reconstructs symmetric and piecewise polynomial tensors on vertex patches in broken $H(\operatorname{div}\operatorname{div})$ spaces.
